text: Common injectable products: Analgin/Dipyrone — good for pain and fever, but short-acting (about 1 hour); inject into muscle, not fat, in pigs to avoid irritation. Phenylbutazone — non-steroidal, active on inflammation, pain, and fever for about 24 hours; also needs careful intramuscular technique. Tolfedine — non-steroidal, active on inflammation/pain/fever for about 48 hours, without causing injection-site irritation. Ketofen (Ketoprofen) — non-steroidal, strong on inflammation, fever, and especially pain, commonly used for musculoskeletal pain from soft-tissue injury, osteoarthritis, or bone/joint problems. Paracetamol — non-steroidal, active on inflammation/pain/fever but only for a few hours, with milder stomach side effects than Ketofen. Dexamethasone — steroidal, strong on inflammation but not on fever or pain; duration depends on the formulation (1 hour to 2 weeks), though products available in Cambodia are generally active about 24 hours. Oral: Paracetamol can also be mixed into feed or water — to boost feed intake in feverish pigs, ease joint/leg pain in sows, support broiler growth in hot weather, and strengthen chicken legs.
